professional [[basketball]] player for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), the [[ABA League|ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]].{{cite web|title='Air' Jordan Nwora came, saw and conquered Nigeria|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/african-qualifiers/news/air-jordan-nwora-came-saw-and-conquered-nigeria|website=FIBA.basketball}}{{cite web|title=Jordan Nwora: Why I chose Nigeria over USA in Basketball|url=https://www.completesportsnigeria.com/jordan-nwora-why-i-chose-nigeria-over-usa-in-basketball/|website=CompleteSportsNigeria.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018|archive-date=August 22, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220822143102/https://www.completesportsnigeria.com/jordan-nwora-why-i-chose-nigeria-over-usa-in-basketball/|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|title=Jordan Nwora - Men's Basketball|url=https://gocards.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7227|website=GoCards.com}}{{cite web|title=Louisville's Jordan Nwora more than just a shooter for Nigerian team|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2018/07/10/jordan-nwora-more-than-just-shooter-nigerian-team/771083002/|website=Courier-Journal.com}} He plays internationally for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team]]. Nwora won a championship with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]] before being traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2023 and again to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2024. ==Early life== Nwora was born on September 9, 1998, in [[Buffalo, New York]] to a Nigerian father{{cite news|url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/basketball/alex-nwora-jordan-nwora-help-expand-sport-of-basketball-give-back-to-communities/article_1aceb736-0ab2-11ed-90b7-4b5234c32d6e.html|title=Alex Nwora, Jordan Nwora help expand sport of basketball, give back to communities|date=July 31, 2022|agency=[[The Buffalo News]]|author=Hricik, Madison|accessdate=October 2, 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220731121824/https://buffalonews.com/sports/basketball/alex-nwora-jordan-nwora-help-expand-sport-of-basketball-give-back-to-communities/article_1aceb736-0ab2-11ed-90b7-4b5234c32d6e.html|archivedate=July 31, 2022}} and an American mother. His father [[Alexander Nwora]], a basketball coach, helped Jordan in developing his basketball abilities.{{cite web |url=https://newtelegraphonline.com/2018/07/playing-for-nigeria-my-decision-not-dads-nwora-basketball-star/ |title=Playing for Nigeria my decision, not dad's –Nwora, basketball star |website=newtelegraphonline.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814232945/https://newtelegraphonline.com/2018/07/playing-for-nigeria-my-decision-not-dads-nwora-basketball-star/ |archive-date=2018-08-14}} ==High school career== Nwora started playing basketball at [[Amherst Central High School]] in the 2013–2014 season, before transferring to [[The Park School of Buffalo]] for two seasons.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jordan-Nwora/Summary/76982#HighSchool|title=Jordan Nwora Player Profile, Milwaukee Bucks, News, Rumors, NBA Stats, NCAA Stats, G League Stats, Events Stats, Game Logs, Bests, Awards - RealGM}} At The Park School he shot 42 percent from three-point range, leading the Pioneers to the New York State Federation Class B championship, averaging 21.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.4 steals, and 1.4 assists. His second season at The Park School saw him raise all of his season averages, turning in 23.4 points, 10.1 rebounds, 2.3 steals, and 1.8 assists. He earned First Team All-Centercourt honors in both his junior{{cite web | url=https://www.theviewfromcentercourt.com/2015/04/the-2015-all-centercourt-team-the-best-in-wny.html | title=The 2015 All-Centercourt Team: The Best in WNY }} and senior{{cite web | url=https://www.theviewfromcentercourt.com/2016/04/the-2016-all-centercourt-team-the-best-in-wny.html | title=The 2016 All-Centercourt Team: The Best in WNY }} seasons playing at The Park School. Nwora continued his prep career for one more season, where he scored over 500 points at Vermont Academy, averaging 18.7 points and 5.3 rebounds in the 2016–2017 season.{{Cite web|url=https://gocards.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7227|title=Jordan Nwora - Men's Basketball}} ==College career== Nwora joined the Louisville Cardinals in 2018. In his freshman season, he averaged 5.7 points, 2.2 rebounds and 0.4 assists per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jordan-nwora-1.html|title = Jordan Nwora College Stats}}{{Cite web|url=http://stats.washingtonpost.com/cbk/players.asp?id=142102|title=Sports}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2018/07/10/jordan-nwora-more-than-just-shooter-nigerian-team/771083002/|title=Louisville's Jordan Nwora more than just a shooter for Nigerian team}} During his sophomore season, Nwora became a permanent starter on the team six games into the season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/louisville/2019-starters.html|title = 2018-19 Louisville Cardinals Starting Lineups}} He averaged 17.0 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game,{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4277883/jordan-nwora|title = Jordan Nwora Stats, News, Bio}} becoming the second Most Improved Player in the NCAA and named Most Improved Player in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]].{{Cite web|url = http://www.sportsviewamerica.com/2019/03/12/college-basketball-louisvilles-jordan-nwora-named-acc-most-improved-player-all-acc/|title = College Basketball – Louisville's Jordan Nwora Named ACC Most Improved Player, All-ACC|date = March 12, 2019|access-date = March 17, 2019|archive-date = March 31, 2022|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220331041115/https://www.sportsviewamerica.com/2019/03/12/college-basketball-louisvilles-jordan-nwora-named-acc-most-improved-player-all-acc/|url-status = dead}} He was named the preseason ACC player of the year. On January 29, 2020, Nwora scored a career-high 37 points and added nine rebounds in a 86–69 win against [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]].{{cite news |title=Nwora scores 37, leads No. 6 Louisville past BC 86–69 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168512 |access-date=January 30, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 29, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Nwora was named to the First Team All-ACC, finishing second in the player of the year voting to [[Tre Jones]].{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}} As a junior, Nwora averaged 18 points and 7.7 rebounds per game while shooting 44% from the field. Following the season, Nwora declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Louisville's Jordan Nwora enters NBA draft after All-America season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29001586/louisville-jordan-nwora-enters-nba-draft-all-america-season |access-date=April 6, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 6, 2020}} He trained at [[Darren Fenn]]'s XGen Elite basketball academy in [[West Seneca, New York|West Seneca]] to keep in shape during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]] and prepare for the draft.{{cite web | last=Rodriguez | first=Miguel | title=Park School product Jordan Nwora hopes to hear his name during NBA Draft | website=Buffalo News | date=November 18, 2020 | url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/high-school/park-school-product-jordan-nwora-hopes-to-hear-his-name-during-nba-draft/article_9d621fc8-293e-11eb-868b-07bc107f7e33.html | access-date=November 3, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2020–2023)=== Nwora was selected with the 45th overall pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Nwora was selected by the Bucks with the 45th overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft. |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-jordan-nwora-drafted-by-bucks-in-round-2/ |website=cbssports.com |date=November 19, 2020 |access-date=November 20, 2020}} On November 24, 2020, the Bucks announced that they had signed Nwora.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Jordan Nwora|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-jordan-nwora|date=November 24, 2020|website=nba.com|access-date=November 24, 2020}} He was assigned to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] for the start of the [[NBA G League]] season, making his debut on February 10, 2021. Three days later, he was recalled from the Stars because of an ankle injury. On May 16, Nwora ended his rookie season by scoring a career–high 34 points on 14–23 shooting, along with 14 rebounds and 2 blocks, during a 118–112 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].[https://www.cardchronicle.com/2021/5/17/22440356/jordan-nwora-drops-career-high-34-points-for-milwaukee Jordan Nwora drops career-high 34 points for Milwaukee] During his rookie season, Nwora became an [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]], helping the Bucks defeat the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2021 NBA Finals]].{{cite news |last1=Williams |first1=Tunde |title=Jordan Nwora wins NBA 2021 Championship with Milwaukee Bucks |url=http://www.brila.net/jordan-nwora-wins-nba-2021-championship-with-milwaukee-bucks/ |access-date=21 July 2021 |work=Latest Sports News In Nigeria |date=21 July 2021}} On December 18, 2021, Nwora scored a season-high 28 points, along with 11 rebounds, in a 119–90 loss to the [[2021–22 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |title=Bucks' Jordan Nwora: Explodes for season-high 28 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-jordan-nwora-explodes-for-season-high-28-points/ |access-date=March 6, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=December 19, 2021 }} He made 62 appearances (13 starts) for Milwaukee during the [[2021–22 NBA season]], averaging 8.7 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jordan Nwora 2021-22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277883/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=February 1, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Nwora played in 38 games (including three starts) for the Bucks during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], logging averages of 6.0 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 1.0 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jordan Nwora 2022-23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4277883/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=February 1, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Indiana Pacers (2023–2024)=== On February 9, 2023, Nwora was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] along with [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]] and [[Serge Ibaka]] in a four-team trade involving the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Acquire Jordan Nwora, George Hill, and Serge Ibaka, and Multiple Second-Round Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-jordan-nwora-george-hill-serge-ibaka-multiple-draft-picks|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}} Nwora joined [[Tyrese Haliburton]], [[Aaron Nesmith]], and [[Jalen Smith]] on the Pacers, and later [[Obi Toppin]], all selected in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. He made his Pacers debut on February 13, recording 7 points, 3 rebounds and 2 steals in a 123–117 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|first=Phillip B.|last=Wilson|title=CLARKSON, MARKKANEN LEAD JAZZ PAST PACERS 123-117|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200859|website=NBA.com|date=February 13, 2023|access-date=February 16, 2023}} On February 25, Nwora recorded 18 points, 8 rebounds, and 6 assists on 8–12 shooting, in a win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=Jordan Nwora (18 Points) Highlights Vs. Orlando Magic|url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/jordan-nwora-18-points-highlights-vs-orlando-magic|website=NBA.com|date=February 25, 2023|access-date=February 25, 2023}} On March 13 against the [[Detroit Pistons]], Nwora recorded 20 points, four rebounds, and two steals.{{cite web|title=Leading scorer against Detroit|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/jordan-nwora-player|website=FOXSports.com|access-date=March 14, 2023}} On March 25 against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Nwora posted a Pacers season–high 33 points and added six rebounds during a loss.{{cite web|title=Explodes for 33 points in loss|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/jordan-nwora-player|website=FOXSports.com|access-date=March 25, 2023}} He scored 25 of his 33 points in the 2nd quarter, setting the Pacers regular–season franchise record for most points in a quarter since tracking began in the [[1996–97 NBA season]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401469262 Collins leads deep Hawks attack in 143-130 win over Pacers]{{cite web|title=Jordan Nwora set the regular-season franchise record for most points in a quarter with 25 points in the second quarter tonight.|url=https://twitter.com/Pacers/status/1639753146464362496?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet|website=Twitter.com|access-date=March 25, 2023}} ===Toronto Raptors (2024)=== On January 17, 2024, the Pacers traded Nwora, along with [[Bruce Brown (basketball)|Bruce Brown]], [[Kira Lewis Jr.]], and three first-round draft picks to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Pascal Siakam]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS COMPLETE TRADE WITH INDIANA|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-complete-trade-with-indiana-2|website=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2024|access-date=January 18, 2024}} Nwora made 34 appearances (one start) for Toronto, recording averages of 7.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. ===Anadolu Efes (2024–2025)=== On August 5, 2024, Nwora signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Jordan Nwora Anadolu Efes'te...|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/haber/jordan-nwora-anadolu-efes-te|website=AnadoluEfesSK.org|date=August 5, 2024|access-date=August 5, 2024|language=tr}}{{cite news|url=https://buffalonews.com/sports/professional/nba/article_4e29cb75-9c73-4342-a4b5-86ec9c9f4241.html|title=A dream on hold: Jordan Nwora finds solace away from the NBA|date=June 19, 2025|agency=''[[The Buffalo News]]''|author=White, Noah|accessdate=June 20, 2025|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250619143658/https://buffalonews.com/sports/professional/nba/article_4e29cb75-9c73-4342-a4b5-86ec9c9f4241.html|archivedate=June 19, 2025}} On October 29, Nwora received Hoops Agents Player of the Week award for Round 4. He had a game-high 35 points, six rebounds and three assists for his team to win.{{cite web |title=Nwora's 35-point game gives him Player of the Week award |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/898744/Nworas-35-point-game-gives-him-Player-of-the-Week-award |website=www.eurobasket.com |access-date=29 October 2024}} ===Crvena zvezda (2025–present)=== On July 8, 2025, Nwora signed with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] of the [[ABA League|ABA League]].{{cite web |title=Jordan Nwora joins Crvena zvezda |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jordan-nwora-joins-crvena-zvezda/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 8, 2025 |date=July 8, 2025}} ==National team career== Nwora was called up to be part of the [[Nigeria national basketball team|D'Tigers]] for the 2019 FIBA world cup qualifier between June 28–30, 2018, by his father Alexander Nwora who is the head coach of the team. In the tournament, he averaged 21.7 points, 8 rebounds and 2.7 assists.{{cite web| url = http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/african-qualifiers/player/Jordan-Nwora| title = International Basketball Federation (FIBA) - FIBA.basketball}} During the 2019 FIBA World Cup qualifiers in Lagos, Nwora scored 36 points against Mali to be the highest scoring player for Nigeria in history,{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/african-qualifiers/news/air-jordan-nwora-came-saw-and-conquered-nigeria|title = 'Air' Jordan Nwora came, saw and conquered Nigeria}} breaking [[Ike Diogu]]'s record of 31 points. Nwora scored a game-high 33 points in a loss to [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]] in the preliminary round of the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Olympics]] in Tokyo. He led Nigeria in scoring in the tournament after averaging 21 points per game.{{cite news |title=Jordan NWORA at the Tokyo 2020 Men's Olympic Basketball Tournament
